levels.title_en: Class 5: feminine nouns not ending in -ी

items.pronunciation_notes: Long aa in the second syllable and a soft final b: ki-taab meṁ.
items.gloss_en: Class 5 singular — no change at all

learn.title_en: The last class, and the quietest one
learn.explanation_en: Class 5 is every feminine noun that does not end in -ी: किताब, रात, बात, चीज़, आवाज़, चाय. These are the words Module 4 made you memorise with their gender attached, because nothing about their shape reveals it. In the singular they behave like almost everything else in this module — they do not change at all. The gender you memorised is not paying off yet. It pays off in the plural, and again when adjectives arrive.

examples.note: Identical to the direct form.
A different postposition, and still nothing happens.

examples.hindi: यह किताब बेटी के लिए है।
examples.read_as: yah kitaab beṭii ke lie hai.
examples.english: This book is for the daughter.
examples.note: किताब is the subject and stays direct; बेटी is the word standing before के लिए.

common_error.why_en: -े is what a Class 1 masculine ending in -ा turns into. किताब is feminine and ends in a consonant, so it takes no ending in the singular.

practice.prompt_en: One book. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: किताब + पर
practice.explanation_en: One book, and Class 5 singulars do not change, so किताब stays as it is.

game.explanation_en: किताबे में invents a masculine ending on a feminine noun. The form is किताब में.

tts_strings: यह किताब बेटी के लिए है।

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable with a retroflex t: raat, then a short ko.

learn.title_en: रात को — ordinary grammar, useful phrase
learn.explanation_en: रात को means at night, and it is worth learning as a phrase because Hindi uses को to place an event in time. But look at what is underneath: a Class 5 feminine noun standing in front of a postposition and doing nothing. There is no special time rule here. The idiom is in the choice of को, not in the shape of रात.

examples.note: The standard way to say when.
Also correct, with a slightly more drawn-out sense.

examples.hindi: मैं रात को घर में हूँ।
examples.read_as: maiṁ raat ko ghar meṁ huuṁ.
examples.english: I am at home at night.
examples.note: Two oblique nouns in one sentence, and neither of them changes shape.

common_error.why_en: रात is feminine and ends in a consonant. There is no -े form for it to take.

practice.prompt_en: One night. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: रात + में
practice.explanation_en: Singular Class 5, so रात is unchanged. रातों is the plural.

game.explanation_en: राते is not a Hindi word. रात does not change in the singular oblique.

tts_strings: मैं रात को घर में हूँ।

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable ending in a glide: chaay, close to the English word chai but with the vowel held.
items.gloss_en: Class 5, and a gender you had to memorise

learn.title_en: Where the memorised gender is still invisible
learn.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, and there is nothing in the word that tells you so — which is exactly why Module 4 flagged it. Here is the honest position: in the singular oblique, the gender does no work at all. चाय behaves like शहर, which is masculine. The gender starts earning its keep one level from now, and it becomes unavoidable when adjectives and की arrive later in this module. Keep holding it; you have not needed it yet.

examples.note: Unchanged, like every Class 5 singular.
के साथ is a postposition, and still nothing happens.

examples.english: There is milk in the tea.
examples.note: दूध is the subject and direct; चाय is the one standing before में.

common_error.why_en: The -े ending belongs to Class 1 masculines. चाय has no ending to convert.

practice.prompt_en: Put this noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: चाय + के साथ
practice.explanation_en: Singular Class 5, so चाय is unchanged before के साथ.

game.explanation_en: चाये में adds an ending that Class 5 nouns never take. The form is चाय में.

summary.recap_en: Class 5 is the feminine nouns ending in a consonant, and in the singular they do nothing. Four of the five noun classes you have met now behave identically here — the singular oblique is really only a Class 1 question.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the Class 5 plural, which takes plain -ों and not the -ियों you learnt for लड़की.

items.pronunciation_notes: The -ों is a hum on the last syllable: ki-taa-boṁ meṁ, four beats in all.
items.gloss_en: Class 5 plural — the ending attaches directly

learn.title_en: The feminine plural that is NOT -ियों
learn.explanation_en: This is the contrast the module has been building towards. लड़की is feminine and its plural oblique is लड़कियों. किताब is also feminine and its plural oblique is किताबों. Same gender, different endings — because लड़की ends in a long -ी and किताब ends in a consonant. So the thing deciding the ending is not the gender at all; it is the last letter. किताबियों does not exist, and a learner who reaches for it has quietly decided that feminine means -ियों.

examples.note: Consonant ending, so -ों goes straight on.
The postposition changes; the noun does not.
A number makes the plural explicit but does not do the work for you.

common_error.why_en: The य and the shortened vowel belong to nouns ending in a long -ी. किताब ends in a consonant, so -ों attaches directly.

practice.prompt_en: More than one book. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: किताब + में
practice.explanation_en: किताबों में. किताबें is the direct plural and cannot stand before a postposition.

game.explanation_en: किताबियों borrows the Class 4 ending. किताब takes plain -ों.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long aa, then the nasal hum: raa-toṁ ko.
items.gloss_en: Class 5 plural on a time noun

learn.title_en: No य, no shortening, nothing in the way
learn.explanation_en: रात becomes रातों, बात becomes बातों, चीज़ becomes चीज़ों. There is no vowel to shorten and no gap for a य to fill, because the word ends in a consonant and -ों can simply follow it. Compare this with आदमियों and लड़कियों, where the य exists only to separate two vowels that would otherwise collide. Once you hear the ending that way, you stop having to remember which nouns take य — you can hear whether one is needed.

examples.note: The plural of the time phrase रात को.
Same class, same plain ending.
तक is a postposition, so the plural must be oblique.

common_error.why_en: There is no vowel here for a य to bridge. The ending goes straight onto the consonant.

practice.prompt_en: More than one. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: बात + में
practice.explanation_en: बातों में. बातें is the direct plural, which cannot stand before में.

game.explanation_en: रातियों adds a य where there is no vowel collision to fix. The form is रातों.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z, not a j: chii-zoṁ meṁ.
items.gloss_en: the two feminine plurals side by side

learn.explanation_en: Put लड़कियों and चीज़ों next to each other and the whole feminine picture resolves. Both nouns are feminine. Both are plural. Both stand before a postposition. And they take different endings, because one ends in -ी and the other in a consonant. If you have been silently using gender to predict the ending, this is the pair that will break the habit — which is worth breaking now rather than at Module 9.

examples.note: Consonant ending, so plain -ों.
The same form before a longer postposition.
And again — the noun's form ignores which postposition follows.

common_error.why_en: Feminine does not mean -ियों. चीज़ ends in a consonant, so it takes -ों like किताब and रात.

practice.prompt_en: More than one thing. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: चीज़ + से
practice.explanation_en: चीज़ों से — plain -ों on a consonant-final feminine noun.

game.explanation_en: चीज़ियों copies the ending that belongs to लड़की. चीज़ takes -ों.

summary.recap_en: Class 5 plurals take plain -ों, with no य and no shortened vowel, because there is no vowel collision to fix. लड़कियों and चीज़ों are both feminine plurals with different endings — the last letter decides, not the gender.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the mixed drill. Every item from here puts two classes in one phrase, so you have to choose rather than apply.

items.pronunciation_notes: और is one syllable, closer to aur than to a-ur: be-ṭe aur be-ṭii ko.
items.gloss_en: two singular nouns, one postposition, two different outcomes

learn.explanation_en: Until now each level handed you a class and asked you to apply it. That is not the real skill. Here both nouns are singular, both are governed by the same को, and one moves while the other does not — because बेटा ends in -ा and बेटी does not. Nothing about the postposition tells you what to do. The last letter of each noun is the only information you are working from, and you have to read it twice in one short phrase.

examples.note: Class 1 moves to -े; Class 4 stays put.
Class 3 and Class 5 — here neither one moves.
The same split as the first example, with a different postposition.

common_error.why_en: को governs both nouns, so बेटा must go oblique even though it is not the word sitting directly in front of the postposition.

practice.prompt_en: Put both nouns into the right form.
practice.question: बेटा + बेटी + को
practice.explanation_en: बेटा goes to बेटे; बेटी stays as it is. Both are covered by the same को.

game.explanation_en: बेटा is Class 1 and must become बेटे, because को governs it too.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two hums in the phrase, one on each noun: laṛ-koṁ aur laṛ-ki-yoṁ ko.
items.gloss_en: the plural version of the same decision

learn.title_en: In the plural, both move — differently
learn.explanation_en: The singular version of this phrase had one noun moving and one standing still. In the plural neither stands still, but they do not move the same way: लड़का takes plain -ों, and लड़की shortens its vowel and takes -ियों. This is the point of the drill. The two nouns are the same length, the same topic, and governed by the same postposition, and the only thing separating their endings is a single letter you have to notice.

examples.note: Plain -ों on one, -ियों on the other.

examples.english: with the children and the girls
examples.note: बच्चा is Class 1, so it takes plain -ों like लड़का.

examples.english: in the houses and the books
examples.note: Class 2 and Class 5 — different genders, and both take plain -ों.

common_error.why_en: Getting the first noun right does not carry over. लड़की still needs its vowel shortened and a य added.

practice.prompt_en: More than one of each. Put both nouns into the right form.
practice.question: लड़का + लड़की + को
practice.explanation_en: लड़कों takes plain -ों; लड़कियों shortens and adds य. लड़काओं keeps a -ा that should have been replaced.

game.explanation_en: लड़कीों stacks -ों on a long ी. It should be लड़कियों.

items.pronunciation_notes: बहनों has a light ह between the vowels: ba-ha-noṁ, and in fast speech it flattens to bah-noṁ.

learn.title_en: The closest pair in the language, and they still differ
learn.explanation_en: भाई and बहन are as close as two nouns get — same family, same register, used together constantly. And their plural obliques are भाइयों and बहनों, because one ends in a long vowel and the other in a consonant. This is the cleanest proof available that the module is about shapes rather than meanings. If meaning decided anything, these two would match. They do not, and no amount of thinking about brothers and sisters will tell you which ending to use.

examples.note: Long vowel takes य; consonant takes the ending directly.
The forms do not depend on the postposition.
Class 5 plural on its own, with nothing to compare it to.

common_error.why_en: Two errors at once: भाई must shorten its vowel, and बहन has no vowel for a य to bridge.

practice.prompt_en: More than one of each. Put both nouns into the right form.
practice.question: भाई + बहन + के साथ
practice.explanation_en: भाइयों shortens and takes य; बहनों takes -ों straight onto the consonant.

game.explanation_en: बहनियों invents a य. बहन ends in a consonant, so the form is बहनों.

summary.recap_en: Every phrase here held two nouns from different classes under one postposition. The lesson is that the class is decided per noun, by its last letter, and getting one right tells you nothing about the other.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the second half of the drill, and the two sentences that compress the whole module.

levels.title_en: Mixed drill: the whole system in two rules

items.pronunciation_notes: Both nouns hold a doubled consonant: kut-toṁ and bil-li-yoṁ.
items.gloss_en: Class 1 and Class 4 in the plural

learn.title_en: Dogs and cats, and two different endings
learn.explanation_en: कुत्ता ends in -ा, so its plural oblique is कुत्तों. बिल्ली ends in -ी, so hers is बिल्लियों. These two words appear together constantly, which makes the pair worth over-drilling: if the phrase comes out automatically, you have internalised the difference between the plain ending and the bridged one rather than working it out each time.

examples.note: Plain -ों, then the bridged -ियों.
Class 1 plural on its own.
Class 4 plural on its own.

common_error.why_en: कुत्ता replaces its -ा rather than adding to it, and बिल्ली shortens its -ी rather than keeping it.

practice.prompt_en: More than one of each. Put both nouns into the right form.
practice.question: कुत्ता + बिल्ली + को
practice.explanation_en: कुत्तों replaces the -ा; बिल्लियों shortens the -ी and bridges with य.

game.explanation_en: कुत्ताओं adds an ending to the direct form instead of replacing the -ा. The plural oblique is कुत्तों.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long vowels running into the short में: paa-nii aur chaay meṁ.
items.gloss_en: the singular rule, stated in full

learn.title_en: In the singular, only Class 1 moves
learn.explanation_en: पानी is masculine Class 3 and चाय is feminine Class 5, and before में both do precisely nothing. That is not a coincidence or a pair of exceptions — it is the general case. Of the five noun classes you have met, exactly one changes in the singular: Class 1, the masculines ending in -ा. Everything else stands still. Say that to yourself as a single sentence, because it turns the singular oblique from five rules into one question: does this noun end in -ा?

examples.english: in the water and the tea
examples.note: Different classes, different genders, and neither one moves.

examples.english: in the yoghurt and the tea
examples.note: Two more that stand still.

examples.english: in the water and the milk
examples.note: Class 3 and Class 2, both unchanged.

common_error.why_en: The -े ending exists only for nouns ending in -ा. Neither of these words qualifies, so neither changes.

practice.prompt_en: Put both nouns into the right form.
practice.question: पानी + चाय + में
practice.explanation_en: Neither noun ends in -ा, so neither changes. Both are mass nouns, so the plural forms do not arise either.

game.explanation_en: पाने applies a Class 1 ending to a Class 3 noun. पानी does not change.

items.pronunciation_notes: बच्चों holds the doubled च: bach-choṁ, and the phrase closes on a long aa in साथ.
items.gloss_en: the plural rule, stated in full

learn.title_en: In the plural, everyone ends in -ों
learn.explanation_en: Every plural oblique in this module ends the same way. The only question is what happens immediately before it. Nouns ending in a long -ी or -ई shorten that vowel and take a य to separate it from the ending: आदमियों, लड़कियों, भाइयों, बिल्लियों. Everything else attaches -ों directly: लोगों, बच्चों, घरों, किताबों, बहनों. Two branches, and the second is the default. Together with the singular rule from the last item, that is the entire module in two sentences.

examples.english: with the people and the children
examples.note: Class 2 and Class 1, both taking the ending directly.

examples.english: to the people and the children
examples.note: The forms are indifferent to the postposition.

examples.english: in the houses and the markets
examples.note: Two more Class 2 nouns, and the same plain ending.

common_error.why_en: बच्चा replaces its final -ा with the ending. Keeping the -ा and adding on top of it is the single most common plural error in this module.

practice.prompt_en: More than one of each. Put both nouns into the right form.
practice.question: लोग + बच्चा + के साथ
practice.explanation_en: लोग is already plural and takes -ों; बच्चा replaces its -ा with the same ending.

game.explanation_en: बच्चाओं keeps the -ा and adds an ending to it. The plural oblique is बच्चों.

summary.recap_en: Two sentences cover every noun in the module. In the singular, only Class 1 moves — the question is simply whether the noun ends in -ा. In the plural, everything ends in -ों, and only nouns with a long final -ी or -ई shorten and take a य before it.
summary.next_up_en: Next: adjectives, where a word can be forced to move even when the noun beside it stands perfectly still.

items.pronunciation_notes: बड़े has the flapped ड़ and ends on a clear e: ba-ṛe ghar meṁ.
items.gloss_en: the adjective moves even when the noun does not

learn.title_en: The word that moves when nothing else does
learn.explanation_en: घर is Class 2 and does nothing before में — you learnt that ten levels ago. But बड़ा is a marked adjective, one that ends in -ा, and marked adjectives go to -े in front of any oblique noun whether or not the noun itself shows a change. So बड़ा घर becomes बड़े घर में, and the entire grammatical signal is carried by the adjective. This is where Module 5's easy postpositions stop being easy: every one of those sentences would have needed this the moment you put a description in front of the noun.

examples.note: घर is unchanged; बड़ा has moved to बड़े.
Any postposition triggers it, not just में.
The noun goes plural and the adjective does not change again — बड़े covers both.

common_error.why_en: The noun does not change, so the adjective is the only thing that can mark the oblique — and it must.

practice.prompt_en: Put the phrase into its oblique form.
practice.question: बड़ा घर + में
practice.explanation_en: बड़ा becomes बड़े; घर is Class 2 and stays as it is.

game.explanation_en: The adjective has been left in its direct form. Before में it must be बड़े.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated chh and retroflex ṭ: chho-ṭe. In शहर the middle vowel almost disappears in speech.
items.gloss_en: one adjective form for singular and plural alike

learn.explanation_en: छोटा becomes छोटे before an oblique masculine noun, and it stays छोटे whether that noun is singular or plural: छोटे शहर में and छोटे शहरों में. The adjective's oblique form and its plural form are the same word, which is one of the few genuinely free things in Hindi grammar — you learn one ending and it covers two jobs. Feminine adjectives work differently, and they arrive in the next level.

examples.note: Singular noun, adjective in -े.
Plural noun, and the adjective is unchanged.
Another Class 2 noun that shows nothing, so the adjective carries it.

common_error.why_en: शहर cannot show the oblique, so the adjective has to. Leaving it as छोटा makes the phrase unmarked.

practice.prompt_en: Put the phrase into its oblique form.
practice.question: छोटा शहर + में
practice.explanation_en: छोटा goes to छोटे; शहर is Class 2 and does not change.

game.explanation_en: छोटा has not been put into the oblique. Before में the form is छोटे शहर में.

items.pronunciation_notes: The doubled च and the aspirated छ run together: ach-chhe, ending on a clear e.
items.gloss_en: the same adjective, direct and oblique, one line apart

learn.title_en: अच्छा becomes अच्छे the moment में appears
learn.explanation_en: The whole exchange turns on one vowel. In the second line the school is the subject, nothing follows it, and the adjective stays direct: अच्छा स्कूल. In the third and fourth lines में is behind it, so the adjective goes oblique: अच्छे स्कूल में. The noun स्कूल is identical in all three lines and tells you nothing. Hearing the same phrase twice with only the adjective changing is the fastest way to feel what the oblique actually marks — it is a relationship between words, not a property of the noun.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: This is a very good school.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: क्या तुम अच्छे स्कूल में हो?
lines.read_as: kyaa tum achchhe skuul meṁ ho?
lines.english: Are you in a good school?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, मैं अच्छे स्कूल में हूँ।
lines.read_as: haaṁ, maiṁ achchhe skuul meṁ huuṁ.
lines.english: Yes, I am in a good school.

common_error.why_en: में makes the noun phrase oblique, and since स्कूल cannot show it, the adjective must.

practice.question: मैं ___ स्कूल में हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: में follows, so the phrase is oblique and the marked adjective takes -े.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: The speaker says अच्छे, because में is standing behind the noun.

tts_strings: क्या तुम अच्छे स्कूल में हो?
हाँ, मैं अच्छे स्कूल में हूँ।

summary.recap_en: A marked adjective — one ending in -ा — goes to -े in front of any oblique masculine noun, singular or plural, and it does so even when the noun itself shows no change at all. In बड़े घर में the adjective is carrying the grammar single-handed.
summary.next_up_en: Next: feminine adjectives, which behave quite differently, and unmarked adjectives that never change at all.
